headline: Signs It Is Time to Call a Professional for Your Vanity Replacement
articleBody:
Swapping out an old vanity might seem simple on the surface, but structural and plumbing obstacles can quickly escalate. Here are clear signals it is time to call a professional contractor:

- Corroded or frozen shutoff valves: If the existing angle stops will not turn completely off or show heavy corrosion, forcing them risks a major leak behind your wallboard.
- Misaligned supply lines and drain rough-ins: New vanities often have fixed shelving, inner drawers, or distinct sink locations that clash directly with your home's existing rough plumbing.
- Unlevel flooring or water damage: If the floor under the old unit is sagging, uneven, or soft from unnoticed moisture leaks, the subfloor needs repair before a new cabinet can sit plumb.
- Local permit triggers: In many jurisdictions, altering supply pipes, electrical outlets, or surrounding wall structures requires formal permitting and licensed oversight.
- Wall anchoring challenges: Floating vanities and heavy hardwood units demand structural backing inside the wall studs to prevent sagging or tear-out over time.

When Professional Guidance Helps
Attempting to force a vanity into place without addressing hidden moisture or mismatched pipe rough-ins can ruin your new cabinetry. An experienced remodeling contractor ensures plumbing, framing, and finishes fit together seamlessly.
